chunks: And Ali ibn al-Husayn informed us through his chain, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abul Jarood, who said: Abu Badr narrated to us, from Olaym, from Salman al-Farisi that he said:

The believers will not cease to be like the bleating of goats, so that the lion does not know which one to lay its hand on; there will be no honor among them to which they refer, nor a pillar to whom they entrust their affairs.
ai.seo_question: What does the metaphor of 'bleating goats' signify regarding the state of believers during the Imam's absence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Salman al-Farisi, transmitted via al-Nu'mani's chain, utilizes the metaphor of a disorganized goat herd to describe the state of the believers during the Major Occultation (al-Ghayba al-Kubra), where the absence of a central authority leads to a loss of distinct leadership and social cohesion. Shia scholars interpret this 'lack of sharaf' (honor/prestige) not as a deficiency in faith, but as a consequence of the Imam's hiddenness, which removes the visible source of guidance and judicial authority, leaving the community in a state of dispersed uncertainty.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (2) Ali bin al-Husayn narrated from Muhammad bin Sinan from Abul Jarood from Abu Badr from Olaym that Salman al-Farisi had said:

“The believers come to a day that they become like the goats. The lion does not know which of them to catch. They will be with no honor nor will they have an assistant, to whom they refer their affairs.”
